newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain's real GDP grows 2.2 percent in 1995.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain's real GDP grows 2.2 percent in 1995.

text.p: Bahrain's gross domestic product (GDP) grew a real 2.2 percent in 1995 compared with 2.4 percent a year earlier, Bahrain Monetary Agency (BMA) figures show.
The BMA, Bahrain's central bank, said in its annual report that GDP at current prices recorded 4.0 percent growth in 1995 compared with 4.6 percent in 1994.
It said value added in the crude oil and natural gas sector rose 11.1 percent in 1995 after a decline of 2.7 percent a year earlier.
The value added of the non-oil sector fell to 2.7 percent in 1995 from 6.0 percent in 1994. The non-oil sector's share of GDP declined to 83.4 percent in 1995 from a previous 84.4 percent.
The contribution of the crude oil and natural gas sector to GDP climbed to 16.6 percent in 1995 from 15.6 percent in 1994, it added.
